senses.gloss:
Kaṅka
poet. Q. in Padyāvalī, v.. 214. 215.

Kaṅka
or katka med. mentioned by the Arabs.
See Reinaud, Mem. Sur. l'Ind. p. 314 ff. Probably identical with Kāṅkāyana. See G. Mukhopadhyaya, HI Med. II. p. 464.

Kaṅkaṇa
poet. Skm. p.. 51. 255. Sbhv. 1085. Vidyākarasahasraka p. 11. A verse of his q. in Ratnakaṇṭha's C. on Kāvyaprakāśa. See Peterson, Intro. Sbhv. p. 14. Peterson thinks he may be Kaṅkaṇavarṣa of Rājataraṅgiṇī, VI. 301. See Kavi Kaṅkaṇa below.

Kaṅkaṇa
Bud.
--Caryādohākoṣagītikā. Cordier II. p. 231.

Kaṅkaṇabandha
citrakāvya (?) by Sudarśanācārya. Mysore I. p. 297.

Kaṅkaṇabandharāmāyaṇa
citrakāvya on Rāmāyaṇa theme; verses composed so a. to form a Kaṅkaṇa. by Kṛṣṇamūrti, son of Gaurī an. Sarvajña of Vāsiṣṭhagotra; with a.'s own C. MT. 2116. 2260 (a.. [Page113-b]

Kaṅkatibrāhmaṇa
Q. Āp. śr. sū. XIV. 20. 4. See p. 103, B. Ghosh, Collections of the fragments of lost Brāhmaṇas, Calcutta, 1935; also Bhagavad Datta, Vaidik Vaṅmay kā Itihās, II. p. 30.

Kaṅkavatīnāmadhāraṇī
Bud. by Jinamitra. Kanjur Kyoto 314.

Kaṅkālatantre
--Mahākālīpūjā. Silchar 13 (inc.). C.. K. mālinītantra.

Kaṅkālatāraṇasādhana
Bud. by Dārikapāda. Cordier II. p. 59.
--C. Ṭīkā, Parahitā by Kumārabodhi. ib. p. 59.

Kaṅkālapurāṇa
Kavīndrācārya 1409.

Kaṅkālabhairavatantra
of the Bhairavāṣṭaka group; ref. to by Lakṣmīdhara in his C. on Saundaryalaharī, Mysore Govt. Ori. Lib. Ser. 11, p. 82, Mysore; also by Gaurīkānta in his C. on same work, Oxf. 108b.

Kaṅkālamālinītantra
of the Dakṣiṇāmnāya; in 50000 verses; dialogue between Śiva an. Pārvatī; mentioned in the Prāṇatoṣiṇī among its source books (1898, Calcutta edn. p. 3). Harsinghji p. 31 (135). L. 246 (inc.). (5 Paṭalas). Mithilā. Nabadwip 498. Ramsingh 1067. SSPC. III. I. 8 (inc.). Tagore 59 (5th Paṭala). Varendra 1005.
Pt.. See IO. Pt.. Bk.. 1938, p. 1247, where it is said to have been printed along with Tantrasāra an. Sulabhatantraprakāśa; perhaps some extracts from it are ptd.
--Gurugītā from. in 9 ślokas (Col. Strīgurugītā). Alph. List Beng. Govt. p. 34. RASB. V. 3306A (2). VIII. B. 6793.
Pt.. See IO. Pt.. Bk.. 1938, p.. 978, 979. [Page114-a.

Kaṅkālamekhalā
Bud.
--Sanātanāvartatrayasukhāgama. Cordier II. p. 244.

Kaṅkālavīrabhadramantra
TD. 17280-94.

Kaṅkālādhyāya
or rasAdhyAya or rasakaGkAlI med. in 21 adhyāyas. by a pupil of Kaṅkālayayogin or Kāṅkāyana.
ACW. 179. 180. BL. 241 (with C.). Filliozat I. 140 (Kāṅkālī Rasaheman). RASB. 16.
Ed. Kas. Skt. Ser. 79, (Āyurveda Section No. 2) with C. Vārttika.
For a Hindi adaptation of the beg. of 16th cent., see below Kaṅkālīgrantha by Nāsīrshāh.
--Vārttika by Merutuṅga of the Añcalagaccha, composed in 1386 A. D.
B. IV. 234. BL. 241 (with text). C.. V. 129. Oudh X. 24. Weber 964.
Pt.. in the above mentioned edn. of text.

Kaṅkālipāda
Bud.
--Ṣoḍaśabindubhāvana. Cordier II. p. 237.

Kaṅkālīgrantha
med. by Nāsīrashāh, the Khaiji ruler of Malwa written between C. A. D. 1500-10. BORI. 1055 of 1886-92. 533 of 1892-95 (inc.). BORI. D. XVI. i. 41. 42. Peters. V. p. 270 (no. 533).
See ABORI. XII. p.. 289-91. The work is a. adaptation with Hindi version of Kaṅkālādhyāya or Rasādhyāya of Kaṅkālayogin noted above.

Kaṅkīrṇatantra
Bud. Skt. Dhāriṇīs. Hod. Bud. 54.

Kaṅkīrṇatantrahṛdayadhāraṇī
Bud. Nepal II. p. 262. Same a. previous ?.

Kaṅkola
--Gaṇapatyārādhana. Oxf. 299b.

Kaṅkhā_Ṭīkā
(new). Bud. one of the texts found in the list contained in a. inscription d. 1442 A. D. a. Pagan. [Page114-b]
See “Pali tracts in inscriptions” in the J. Myth. Soc. XXII, p. 410; Bode, Pāli Lit. of Burma p. 102.

Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī
Bud. Pāli. name of C. by Buddhaghoṣa on Pātimokkha of the Vinayapiṭaka.
Br. Mus. Pāli p.. 137. II. p. 108. Cabaton II. 15. Copen. Pāli p. 147. Fausbo7ll 7. 26. 148. Paris Pali p. 32.
--C.. a.. Līnathapakāsinī. Gandhavaṁsa JPTS. 1886, p.. 62. 72.
Pt.. Rangoon, 1903.
--C.. Vinayatthamañjūsā by Buddhanāga. Written a. the instance of Sumedha. Fausbo7ll 28.
Ed.. Colombo, 1901-15.

Kāṅkāyana
interlocutor in Atharvapariśiṣṭa Bṛhallakṣahoma XXXI (Weber 365, p. 91); XXXb, Leipzig edn.

Kāṅkāyana
ancient authority on med. who belonged to Bāhlīka. ref. to in Carakasaṁhitā I. 1, 25, 26 (a. foremost physician of Bāhlīka) an. IV. 6. Different medical formulae are attributed to Kāṅkāyana in texts, Gadanigraha etc.-Kā. guṭika, ºmodaka, ºvaṭaka an. ºvirecana (the last in Bower ms. XI. p. 166). See G. Mukhopadhyaya, HIMed. II. p.. 463-6. Q. by Niścalakara in his C. on Cikitsāsaṅgraha. See IHQ. XXIII. p. 140.
Probably identical with Kaṅka or Katka of the Arabs. See Reinaud, Mem. sur l'Ind., p. 314 ff., Mukhopadhyaya, HIMed. II. p. 464.

Kāṅkāyanavaṭikā
med. by Naravata. K. 212. See above under Kāṅkāyana.

Kāṅkālī
--Rasaheman. med. Filliozat I. 140. See above Kaṅkālādhyāya.
